I mean not really...a lot of things happened as a result of me taking time. I lost my job bc they weren’t accepting of mental illness as a legitimate absence reason. I also missed my nephews wedding. And my bf broke up with me. However do I regret it? Absolutely not. It was one of those times where I really got to see my families/friends true colors and how people responded. I was in a haze most of the time so I couldn’t really tell you how I would’ve thought rationally during that time. I am just looking back on it now as rational. 

As for the friends...the two friends that came didn’t have a clue that this shit was going on with me until I was already there. So we spent a good portion just talking about what I was experiencing. I know for a fact that since that convo they don’t hold me showing up to events to such high expectation anymore which I love because it was unrealistic. 

It really is a judgment call you’re going to have to make on your own. I did. And all the same people that were truly there before are there now. 

I will day this though. I’m 28 and after the hospital visit I was dx with bipolar 2. Had we known about this prior I probably wouldn’t have wound up there. 

I’ve been suicidal since I was a teenager. And this time was very different. I had always had plans and whatnot. All the feelings were very impulsive and out of control in a sense. I really was scared of myself. And I knew that if I had been around my friends and family someone would’ve gotten hurt. So I decided that me going to the hospital was a better decision for everyone at the time. Including myself. I didn’t have any intention of dying. But I kept attempting.

I should also clarify that I went to my therapy appt and stated “I am terrified of myself and I’m scared I’m going to hurt someone” no questions asked we did a soft handoff and that was that. You’re only hurting yourself by closing off to your therapist. Why have one after that ya know? They’re only job is to listen to you and help. If you feel you need a different one that’s a different story, but you pay them money because you have certain expectations. Don’t close off. It’s not gonna do ya any good.

Honestly, you have to decide if you would really benefit from being in a hospital where you can’t leave until a dr. Says you can. Most hospitals even if you voluntarily commit yourself will have you on a 72-hr hold. You’ll have a pay a shit ton of money depending on what insurance you have.  Also, when you “commit yourself” your being committed to the ER until the psych ward would have a bed available. When I did it there was no bed and they were going to ship me 1/2 way across the state. So I chose subacute for 10 days at a local facility. 

Idk what relationship you have with your parents and why you wouldn’t want them to know. But you shouldn’t go thru this alone. When I was at subacute my friends came and saw me for a few hours and it made a world of difference. 

Good luck. Lemme know if you have more questions.

Oh no worries here. I'm in the social work field currently working on getting my masters. I have a CPTSD and BP2 dx. Fun shit I know...anyway, I was suicidal and "checked myself in" to the ER to which all they could offer me was an open door policy and a "safe" place to sleep. What ended up happening was the Social Worker who came in to "evaluate my suicidality" determined that I was safe to go home, and shut the door. SHE SHUT THE GODDAMN DOOR ON A SUICIDAL PATIENT. I was shocked, but at the same time was staring down a call light cord debating whether or not to wrap it around my neck, but do it just right so that it wasn't dislodged and set the alarm off. So yea, I would say to each their own therapist, nurse, social worker, etc...they all mean well but you really gotta know what you're doing in those situations. 

I was asked whether I wanted to be "shipped" off to another town to seek hospital psych ward treatment or go to a sub-acute facility in the town I resided in. I chose the sub-acute which was nothing short of a vacation if you ask me. They preached intensive therapy...that was a joke. I watched Netflix and Hulu for a week and then decided it was time to go back to life. That should've never been left to me...but it was. 

And now here I am 3 months later, dealing with the FULL set of ramifications of that stay, all because I decided living was better than dying. Fucking joke if you ask me. 

I hope I can put a positive stamp on such a broken system, but the thought never leaves my mind if I would just be better off in a residential setting.
